title: Fish Pie
subtitle: A classic British fish pie with a fluffy mashed potato top
excerpt: Fish pie is one of the great British comfort dishes. Chunks of salmon, cod, and prawns sit in a creamy parsley sauce under a golden mashed potato crust. It takes a little effort but nothing complicated.
sourceNotes: Fish pie has been a British staple since at least the Victorian era. The combination of mixed fish in a white sauce under potato is the most recognisable version today.

recipe.freezeNotes: Assemble but do not bake. Cover and freeze for up to 2 months. Bake from frozen at 200C for 55 to 60 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the pie up to 24 hours ahead and refrigerate. Add 10 minutes to the baking time.

content.text: Do not add the raw fish directly to a very hot sauce. Arrange it in the dish first, then pour the warm sauce over. It will cook through fully during baking.

Cook the potatoes in a large pan of salted boiling water for 15 to 18 minutes until completely tender. Drain well, then mash with the 20g of butter and a splash of milk until smooth. Season generously.
Preheat the oven. Make the white sauce: melt the remaining 40g of butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and stir for 2 minutes to cook out the raw taste.
Add the milk a little at a time, whisking constantly after each addition. Once all the milk is in, add the cream. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring often, until thick and smooth.
Remove from the heat. Stir in the parsley, dill, and lemon juice. Season well.
Arrange the raw fish and prawns in a large baking dish (about 30cm x 22cm). Pour the sauce evenly over the top.
Spoon the mash over the fish. Spread it to the edges and rough up the surface with a fork.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the mash is golden and the sauce is bubbling at the edges.

items.cause: Milk was added too fast without whisking.
items.fix: Strain through a sieve and whisk vigorously over low heat.

items.symptom: The mash top has sunk into the filling.
items.cause: The mash was too loose or was spread over hot sauce.
items.fix: Cool the sauce slightly before topping; use firm mash.

items.cause: It was overcooked; the prawns are most vulnerable.
items.fix: Check at 30 minutes; the filling is done when bubbling at the edges.
